title: CourseGraph
description: Stage 2 output. The learning-objective graph extracted from uploaded course content. This is the intermediate representation the whole system rests on: it is the input to narrative planning, the vocabulary for scene generation, and the blueprint for assessment. Produced by one structured-output call over the ingested document.

graph_id.description: Stable id. Games reference this so a regenerated game can be traced to the extraction it came from.

segment_count.description: How many chunks ingestion produced. Every source_span segment_id must be less than this.

concepts.description: Upper bound is a cost guardrail, not a pedagogical claim. Long documents are extracted section by section.

concept_id.description: Slug derived from the label. Must be unique within the graph.

label.description: Human readable name as it appears to the learner.

summary.description: One or two plain sentences. This is what the learner must end up understanding, not a definition copied from the source.

bloom_level.description: Drives which scene mechanic is appropriate. remember and understand map to dialogue plus prediction; apply and above map to simulation.

prerequisites.description: Concepts that must be taught before this one. Must be acyclic. The narrative planner topologically sorts on this field, so a cycle is a hard failure, not a warning.

source_spans.description: Grounding. Every concept must point at the text it came from. A concept with no span is a hallucination and is dropped.

misconceptions.description: The highest value field in the schema. These become the distractors in prediction scenes. Plausible wrong beliefs a learner actually holds, not arbitrary wrong answers.

quote.description: Verbatim text from the segment. Validation checks this string actually occurs in the segment. If it does not, the concept is rejected.

statement.description: The wrong belief, written in the learner's voice as something they would actually think.

why_plausible.description: Why a reasonable learner lands here. Used to write the reveal text so the correction addresses the actual reasoning error.

correction.description: What is actually true and why. Shown after the learner commits.
